the reaction mechanism of oxygen reduction at W/DCE interface by 1, 2-diferrocenyethane (DFcE), as well as by other ferrocenes, is not a simple one-electron process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the reduction of molecular oxygen and hydrogen peroxides by 1,3-diferrocenylpropane at a polarized W/DCE interface follows a PCET mechanism and that the reaction is slow due to the low thermodynamic driving forces.
DFcE can act as a mediator for O2 and H2O2 reduction in a two phase system, and that the reaction is limited by proton transfer across the interface.

the reduction of oxygen and hydrogen perioxide at the W/DCE interface is slow and the rate determining step in both cases is the protonation step of DFcE, followed by the electron transfer to form DFcE–.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reduction of oxygen and hydrogen peroxides at liquid/liquid interfaces is possible, but the rate of these reactions is limited by the slow protonation of DFceE.
PCET reactions can be studied in the W/DCE system and the W/DCE interface can be used to study the PCET reactions in the oil phase.

the reduction of oxygen at liquid/liquid interfaces is a slow process that is limited by the protonation of the organic phase, which in turn depends on the proton concentration in the aqueous phase and the interfacial proton transfer rate.
